chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Jibraeel came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Live as you wish, for you will surely die; love whom you wish, for you will surely part from him; and do as you wish, for you will surely meet [your deeds/God].'

key_terms.لَاقِيهِ: Meeting him (referring to deeds or God)

ai.seo_question: What did the angel Jibraeel tell Prophet Muhammad about life, love, and deeds?
ai.summary: In this renowned hadith from al-Kafi, Jibraeel conveys a triad of existential truths to the Prophet Muhammad, linking the transient nature of life, love, and deeds to the certainty of death and the ultimate encounter with God. Shia scholars often interpret this as a call to mindful living, where freedom of choice is balanced by the accountability of one's actions in the Hereafter. The message underscores that while humans have agency in how they live and whom they love, they are inevitably bound to meet their Creator.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Live as you<sup>saww</sup> wish but you<sup>saww</sup> will certainly die; love whoever you<sup>saww</sup> wish, but you<sup>saww</sup> will certainly depart from him, and act as you<sup>saww</sup> wish but one day you<sup>saww</sup> will face your deeds.’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Jibril (Gabriel) came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘O Muhammad, live as you wish, but you will certainly die; love whoever you wish, but you will certainly depart him, and act as you wish but one day you will face your deeds.’”
